name: Fiji
summary: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag in the canton and the shield of Fiji's coat of arms in the fly. A 2015 plan to replace it was abandoned after Fiji's rugby sevens team won Olympic gold in 2016.
origin: The flag was adopted at independence from Britain on 10 October 1970, based on the colonial blue ensign but with a lighter blue.

In 2015 Prime Minister Frank Bainimarama announced the Union Flag would be removed, and a competition was held. The plan was dropped in 2016, partly in recognition of Fiji's Olympic rugby sevens victory under the existing flag.

symbols.name: Shield of the arms
symbols.description: A white shield with a red cross; a golden lion holding a cocoa pod in the chief; sugar cane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove with an olive branch in the quarters.
symbols.meaning: Fiji's agriculture and peace; the lion and cross recall Britain.

facts: Fiji won its first-ever Olympic medal, a gold in rugby sevens, at Rio 2016.
Fiji's light blue is one of the lightest blues used on a blue ensign.
The shield includes a dove of peace, a symbol from King Cakobau's 1871 flag.
clues: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag and a shield showing a lion, sugar cane, a palm and a dove.
A plan to remove its Union Flag was dropped after an Olympic rugby victory.
Its shield shows bananas and a coconut palm.
